features.name: Net Square
features.now: Presence works: the server, the transports on every system, and a prototype Square where other players walk as NPCs.
features.left: Move the way in to a gate in Lan's HP, rebuild the Square from BN6's own pieces, and make the people in it talkable.

features.name: Trade
features.now: Designed: counters at Trade Central in the Square, the server commits a trade, and the swap is applied after the visit returns, with BN6's own give and take chips.
features.left: All of it: the counters, the server's commit, the swap in the live game, and a pending file that holds CONTINUE until the trade settles.

features.name: Arena
features.now: NetBattles from the Net Square between two games, each running both linked cores, only keys crossing the server, the pair hashed every 60 frames. Full rules for two games with BN5's ROM: BN5's installs written down as the game's core makes them and made again in both pair cores, BN5's chips and Souls carried; UNITE's Soul carried to the other GBA by the pair. Proven on two clients: MrkCan1 and KnightSoul on both screens with every hash agreeing.
features.left: The other five Souls, Chaos Unison, ColonelSoul's button and BN5's mood in a NetBattle seen on both GBAs; a marker that wanders against a moving target checked against BN5; rollback.

features.name: Two MegaMen a side
features.now: Behind --dev arena2v2: four MegaMen on BN6's field in the Arena's pair, the partners' keys two more streams of the Arena's input (players 2 and 3), sampled on their side's GBA's frames, queued in both cores' RAM at that GBA's battle-loop iteration plus BN6's own delay and taken at the key copy by each GBA's own iteration; guessed and rolled back as the other player's. Each MegaMan's HP is his own object's; side 0's partner has his own battle NaviStats, answered by object (him and what he spawns) at BN6's NaviStats routine.
features.left: The streams over the server (the wire's four seats, designed in ONLINE_ARENA.md); side 1's partner's record (RAM for a second record, and both partners' hands, not yet found free: a survey of BN6's RAM in a NetBattle); his own hand and Custom screen (designed); his HP box on his own GBA.

changes.what: The trade machinery and the save gate it put on every run came out of the game; Trade starts again from its design.
The Arena research was trimmed to what the production Arena builds on: the linked pair, the input wire, the Practice script and the pair's snapshot. `build.py online-pair` runs them.
The link cable's findings are one page, docs/ONLINE_LINK.md.
This status is written by tools/re_status.py from docs/re/ledger.json.
Full rules: the Arena's pair holds BN5's installs (src/emu/xinstall_log.c) and carries a united Soul to the other GBA (src/online/arena_souls.c).

--dev arena2v2's partners are streams of the Arena's input (src/online/arena_input.c, arena_link_local.c, arena_pair.c), queued by the battle's iteration in core RAM (RAM_TEAM_RING, src/online/arena_team.c).
--dev arena2v2: side 0's partner's own battle NaviStats (RAM_TEAM_NAVI, src/online/arena_team_navi.c), answered by object; teamhp=N and arenaother for its proof.

experiments.name: Two games through the hosted server
experiments.result: The same room built from seed 120 on both; 211 peer positions matched; round trips 33 to 49 ms; both MegaMen back unchanged, all 24 checkpoint files unchanged.
experiments.meaning: Presence over the public internet works, and a visit leaves the save alone.

experiments.name: Sixteen games, two full channels
experiments.result: 10,248 peer positions matched; every game's loadout back after a disconnect; 192 checkpoint files unchanged.
experiments.meaning: A full room holds on one machine; not a measure of handhelds or a busy network.

experiments.name: Browser and native game together
experiments.result: Both built the same room; 578 browser and 592 native peer positions matched.
experiments.meaning: The browser build can share a Square with the native ones.

experiments.name: Retroid Pocket Nova on the public server
experiments.result: Same room as a desktop peer; 189 handheld positions matched; round trips 40 to 47 ms; a 1,000 HP checkpoint back unchanged.
experiments.meaning: The PortMaster build visits as the desktop does; the only physical handheld tried.

experiments.name: Spare chips read from the Pack
experiments.result: Six folder scenarios through BN6's own folder editor agreed with the reader; six planted faults caught.
experiments.meaning: Which copies are spare (the Pack less every folder's copies) can be read exactly; the rule is kept at commit 7b4b8ef.

experiments.name: ROM-free cable on every desktop and the Nova
experiments.result: 256 transfers and all 1,024 received words right on Linux, Windows x64, macOS ARM64 and the Nova.
experiments.meaning: mGBA's lockstep cable links two cores on every system tried.

experiments.name: Practice on one pair of cores
experiments.result: BN6's Practice unpatched: 18,855 serial transfers, 100 to 0, both back at the menu, all 1,433 battle frames agreeing.
experiments.meaning: BN6's own NetBattle runs on two linked cores without help.

experiments.name: Serial words sent over a socket
experiments.result: Completes at no delay; at 50, 100 and 150 ms only 95, 48 and 35 battle frames in a minute.
experiments.meaning: The cable cannot be split across the network.

experiments.name: Inputs only, two cores per client
experiments.result: Completes at 0, 50, 100 and 150 ms one-way delay, every battle timer as the original; a flipped input and a killed peer both stop the fight.
experiments.meaning: The Arena's design: each client runs both games, only inputs travel.

experiments.name: Snapshot of the pair
experiments.result: Restored at six points and replayed 1, 4 and 8 frames, twice each: every replay exact; 863,016 bytes, 1.2 ms a restore on the desktop.
experiments.meaning: Rollback is possible, but only with more than mGBA's own state save.

experiments.name: A carried chip in the pair
experiments.result: Cannon A, given by BN6's own routine, chosen and hitting for 40 in Practice.
experiments.meaning: A run's chip fights natively; the installer for a whole loadout is still to build.

experiments.name: BN5 in both pair cores, two clients
experiments.result: The same installs' record on both (1,913,709 bytes, 132 hooks) and the same ready hash; Alpha's MrkCan1 took Beta from 100 to 30 on both screens, every hash agreeing to the end; a desync and two records apart each stopped both.
experiments.meaning: Two games with BN5's ROM make byte-identical pairs from their own ROMs; a difference in the installs is caught at the ready.

experiments.name: UNITE across the cable
experiments.result: Both GBAs number the sides alike (BN6_BATTLE_SIDE 0 on the challenger's core, 1 on the other's); with the committed Soul carried at the frame's end both cores read side 0 in form 8 with Soul 11 from the same frame, and both screens drew KnightMan's summon and KnightSoul, 36 hashes agreeing.
experiments.meaning: BN6's link carries the form and not the Soul; the pair carries the Soul, and the look is drawn by the side the sprite selector's caller draws.

experiments.name: Two MegaMen a side (epic #167's spike)
experiments.result: With a side's second MegaMan's keys written at the battle loop's key copy (0x08012DFC) by the loop's iteration, both GBAs' battles agree at every iteration: the research harness over a whole battle (every T1, T3 and T4 object, AI data, NaviStats, hand and random number compared; nothing apart beyond BN6's own 1v1's fields) and the pair under --dev rollbench,arena2v2 (489 iterations, 0 apart, 11 rollbacks the same); one key flipped on one GBA parts them (325 apart). The feasibility study's one-frame skew was its harness: every mode it ran was mode 1, which scheduled the partner by each core's own frame counter, a frame or two apart at the same iteration.
experiments.meaning: BN6's engine runs two MegaMen a side alike on both GBAs; a partner's keys must enter by the battle's iteration. Under full rules BN5's chip AI gave both of side 0's MegaMen one AI data block, which the flag keeps to the first.

experiments.name: Two MegaMen a side: the partners as streams
experiments.result: --dev arena,arenaboth,arena2v2=1 at delay 1: with 107 rollbacks (lag 4, window 8) and with none (lag 0) the battle ends at frame 2690 with all 44 hashes the same; the GBAs agree at all 2,399 iterations, 0 of the partners' takes late; arenaroll=8 rolls back 335 times, the game's state the same each time, its 44 hashes the delay alone's; a key flipped on the second GBA at iteration 300 parts the GBAs at 2,100 iterations. A NetBattle without the flag ends as before (frame 2690, 86d2f837337a1494).
experiments.meaning: A partner's keys can cross a network as a stream of their own and enter BN6 at the battle's iteration on both GBAs; rollback covers them since the rings are core RAM.

experiments.name: Two MegaMen a side: the partner's own NaviStats
experiments.result: With BN6's battle NaviStats routine (0x08013682) answered by object for the five routines that pass the object in r5, side 0's partner reads and writes his own record: given 150 max HP he is set up with 150 while his lead keeps 100, a hit takes him 100 to 90 while his lead stays at 100, the second GBA's screen shows his own HP under him; both GBAs agree at all 2,399 iterations, with 107 rollbacks and without them all 44 hashes the same, arenaroll=8 335 of 335 the same; his record on one GBA alone parts them from iteration 1; with the record his side's copy the battle's 194 hits are those without the hook.
experiments.meaning: BN6's one-NaviStats-a-side is answered by object without touching its code; the RAM the project has free holds one record, so the second partner's waits on a RAM survey.

method.target: BN6 Gregar USA, SHA-1 89fe0bac4fd3d2ab1d2ca35e87ef8b1294a84cd6, on mGBA 0.10.5 (docker/mgba.sh pins its source)
method.oracle: The unpatched game on a fresh pair of cores from the same boot-3.state, run again for each experiment
rules: The player's ROM is only read; saves, states and traces stay under .build/.
Network work runs against the project's own server and the developer's own games, never anyone else's service or account.
No masks: a difference between the original and ours is explained or it fails.
No Tango code is read or used.

glossary.meaning: The online place players visit between acts; other players walk in it as NPCs.
BN6's own homepage map, where MegaMan arrives after every act; the Square's gate is to stand there.
The Square's counters where two players are to swap chips.
NetBattles between players, BN6's own fights over the network.
Two mGBA cores joined by an emulated link cable, both games running on one client.
BN6's NetBattle choice that costs no chip; the fight every experiment scripts.
Each frame waits until both players' inputs for it have arrived.
Run ahead on a guessed input, then rewind to a snapshot and replay when the real one arrives.
Everything needed to resume the pair exactly: both cores, both flash saves, the cable.
The unchanged original, run the same way, that ours is compared against.
A deliberate break, to show the comparison catches it.
The game's own state after boot, before a run changes anything; made on each machine, never committed.
